text:
Arseny Gritsyuk was a fifth-round pick in 2019 who spent years in the KHL, and in his second NHL season he looks like a real top-nine forward for New Jersey. He has 8 goals and 17 points in 22 games on almost 16 minutes a night, already more than half of last season's 31 points.

The Devils love having him out there. They get about 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, four points better than when he sits. Some of the scoring is running ahead of the chances (8 goals on 5.6 expected, and his teammates are finishing above their looks too), so the raw totals flatter him a little. The play driving doesn't.

His style is built for speed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries last season, and more than half his shots came off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins as a rookie. He's gone five games without a goal while setting up four, and his minutes have climbed. We'd watch whether the finishing holds as the role grows.
